text:
Charlie McAvoy has played 11 of Boston's 17 games, and in those games the Bruins have looked like a different team. With him on the ice at 5v5 they take 61.9 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 12 points better than when he sits. He is playing 24:42 a night against the other team's best, which is the job Evolving-Hockey's numbers said he did last season too, when his competition ranked in the 95th percentile and he was worth 1.8 wins.

The points are all assists: 8 in 11 games, including four assists against Nashville. One goal on 1.54 expected is about right for a defenseman whose game is moving the puck to someone else. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 83rd percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists.

Markerzone had him and Trevor Connelly sparking a Bruins and Golden Knights brawl this week, so the edge is still there. The thing to watch is his availability. Boston is a better team when he is in the lineup, and the gap is not small.
headline: McAvoy is driving Boston when he plays
